  • Du leitest unsere Design-Praktikanten und Berufseinsteiger fachlich an, gibst Feedback am Handwerk und baust darauf perspektivisch dein eigenes Team auf.

  • Du arbeitest in einem Umfeld, das hierarchisch in der Entscheidung, flach in der Kommunikation und autonom in der Ausführung ist. Leistung wird gefeiert, nicht versteckt — wer vorankommen will, weil er gut ist, findet hier den Raum dafür, ohne politische Tarnung und ohne Konsens-Theater.

Deine Perspektiven

Was du nach 6 Monaten geliefert hast:

  • Du hast das visuelle System ausgebaut — Typografie, Farbe, Bildsprache und Komponenten sind erkennbar weiterentwickelt, nicht nur inventarisiert.

  • Du hast vogel-beratung.com überarbeitet, die neuen Seiten sind live.

  • Du bist der zentrale Ansprechpartner für alle Designthemen im Unternehmen — Anfragen laufen bei dir zusammen, statt bei Externen zu landen.

  • Du lieferst konstanten Output an Assets über alle Kanäle, ohne dass Themen liegen bleiben.

  • Die Marke beginnt, deine Handschrift zu tragen.

Was du nach 12 Monaten geliefert hast:

  • Das Designsystem ist in Figma so aufgesetzt, dass Content-, Growth- und Recruiting-Themen ohne dich sauber daraus produzieren.

  • Die täglichen Assets aus dem Beratungsalltag — Präsentationen, Slides, Mandantenunterlagen — entstehen automatisiert per KI auf Basis deines Designsystems. Dass das trägt, hängt an sauberer Dokumentation und einem belastbaren technischen Setup: beides liegt bei dir.

  • Das Designsystem und die Assets aller Sub-Marken der Vogel-Gruppe sind ausgebaut und angewendet — jede Marke hat ein eigenes visuelles Fundament, das erkennbar aus derselben Logik kommt.

  • Dein Partner-Setup steht: ausgewählte Agenturen und Kreativpartner, klare Briefing-Standards, Qualitätsurteil bei dir.

  • Motion Design läuft als eigener Produktionsstrang unter deiner Steuerung.

Was du nach 24 Monaten geliefert hast:

  • Vogel ist visuell unverwechselbar — im Markt zuordenbar, ohne dass ein Logo nötig ist.

  • Eine neue Marke setzt du visuell in Wochen auf, nicht in Quartalen — das System trägt das, ohne dass du jedes Asset selbst baust.

  • Du hast mindestens einen Junior-Designer eingestellt, eingearbeitet und auf ein Niveau gebracht, auf dem er eigene Strecken trägt.

Wohin sich die Stelle entwickelt:

Der nächste Schritt ist die fachliche Führung von Design und Brand über alle Marken hinweg (IC-Karriere) — das setzt ein visuelles System voraus, das ohne dich trägt, nicht nur zusätzliche Berufsjahre. Wenn du das Team mit aufbaust und führen willst, öffnet sich zusätzlich die Führungslaufbahn. Wir kennen keinen Automatismus „mehr Erfahrung gleich höhere Stufe".

Das bringst du mit

Erfahrung & Track Record

  • Du hast ein Portfolio auf höchstem Niveau — Grafikdesign, Typografie, Branding-Systeme, visuelles Storytelling. Das Portfolio entscheidet, nicht der Lebenslauf.

  • Du hast in einem professionellen Setup produziert: Agentur mit Design- oder Branding-Fokus, eigenes Studio, oder Inhouse bei einer Marke mit starkem visuellem System. Berufsjahre sind für uns ein Indiz, kein Kriterium — wir entscheiden an Arbeiten und an Umsetzungsfähigkeit.

  • Du hast Kommunikationsdesign, Grafikdesign, visuelle Kommunikation oder Vergleichbares studiert — oder du hast dir das Handwerk selbst beigebracht und kannst das mit Arbeiten belegen, die den Abschluss ersetzen.

  • Profile, die nicht in das obige Raster passen, aber visuelles Urteil und Umsetzungstiefe mitbringen, sind ausdrücklich eingeladen — wir bewerten am Beitrag, nicht am Etikett. Konkret: Designer aus einem kleinen Studio ohne große Namen, dessen Arbeiten besser sind als das, was große Agenturen abliefern; Art Director aus einem Feld weit weg von B2B — Mode, Kultur, Gastronomie, Musik — mit systemischem Denken; Architekt oder Szenograf mit ausgeprägtem Gespür für Typografie und Fläche; Autodidakt mit eigenem Magazin, Label oder Projekt, das visuell trägt. Die ausgewiesene Range ist auf das Primärprofil ausgelegt. Wer einen anderen Hintergrund mitbringt, startet zu einem anderen Marktpreis und konvergiert nach zwölf Monaten bewährter Leistung auf das Rollen-Niveau — die Logik dahinter steht in unseren Vergütungsgrundsätzen.

Skills & Arbeitsweise

  • Du beherrschst die Adobe Creative Cloud auf Produktionsniveau — InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop — und Figma als Systemwerkzeug.

  • Du kannst Webdesign so übergeben, dass es umsetzbar ist. Ein Grundverständnis von HTML und CSS hilft, ist aber keine Voraussetzung.

  • Du hast Motion-Grundlagen — genug, um zu briefen, zu steuern und Ergebnisse zu beurteilen. Mehr ist willkommen.

  • Du arbeitest mit KI als selbstverständlichem Werkzeug — Bildgenerierung, Varianten-Exploration, Retusche, schnelles Durchspielen von Layout-Richtungen. Du denkst ein Designsystem so, dass eine KI verlässlich daraus produzieren kann. Repetitive Aufgaben sind dir ein Reiz zur Automatisierung, kein Schicksal.

  • Du produzierst in kurzen Zyklen und zeigst früh Unfertiges. Lange Abstimmungsschleifen und Präsentations-Choreografie brauchst du nicht.

Mindset & Persönlichkeit

  • Du hast Geschmack und erkennst, wann etwas gut ist, ohne dass jemand dir Kriterien vorgibt — und du kannst deine Entscheidung trotzdem begründen, statt dich hinter Geschmack zu verstecken.

  • Du hältst eine gestalterische Position, wenn du überzeugt bist, und lässt sie fallen, wenn das Gegenargument besser ist.

  • Du willst mit Menschen arbeiten, die Design verstehen und nicht erst überzeugt werden müssen, dass es zählt. Die Feedback-Runden gehen hier über die Sache, nicht über Geschmackspolitik.

  • Du hast den Anspruch, in allem, was du ablieferst, den höchsten Standard zu setzen — nicht weil jemand es kontrolliert, sondern weil Mittelmaß dich persönlich stört.

Was du bei uns nicht finden wirst

  • Kein Job, in dem du Design an Agenturen abgibst und Reportings durchsiehst. Du produzierst selbst. Partner kommen dazu, wo Kapazität oder Spezialisierung fehlt — nicht anstelle deiner Handschrift.

  • Kein Hochglanz-Agentur-Workflow. Wir iterieren in kurzen Zyklen, entscheiden am Bildschirm und schrauben am Detail selbst. Wer Vorlauf, Abstimmungskaskaden und Präsentations-Rituale braucht, arbeitet hier gegen den Takt.

  • Kein Greenfield-Design in einem leeren Raum. Vogel hat ein bestehendes Erscheinungsbild, laufende Mandantenkommunikation und eine Website, die produktiv ist. Was du baust, muss neben dem laufenden Betrieb funktionieren.

  • Kein Marketing-Korsett, in dem du auf Beförderungen wartest. Wachstum entsteht hier am Beitrag, nicht am Berufsjahr — und nicht daran, wie viele Menschen an dich berichten.

  • Kein Ausstieg in eine 40-Stunden-Woche und kein Remote-First-Setup. Die Intensität bleibt hoch, anders gerichtet und mit deutlich mehr Ownership. Diese Rolle braucht Präsenz in München — Design entsteht hier im Raum mit anderen.

FAQ

1. Was ist Vogel — und wo arbeitet ihr?

Vogel ist eine der führenden Mittelstandsberatungen Deutschlands — Familienunternehmen seit 1959, aus Aalen — und baut daraus die führende Beratungsplattform für den Mittelstand. Wir wachsen an mehreren Standorten: in Aalen/Ostwürttemberg als gewachsenem Stammsitz und in München als neuem Hub. An beiden suchen wir quer durch die Funktionen — von Steuerberatung über Beratung bis zu den strategischen Teams, die die Plattform bauen.

2. Wie sind die Gehaltsbänder zu verstehen?

Bewusst breit — und an jeder Stelle ausgewiesen. Wir differenzieren nach Track Record und Marktwert, nicht nach Abschluss: knappe, stark gefragte Profile am oberen Ende, weniger knappe am unteren. Wir kalibrieren ausschließlich am Markt — zwei Menschen mit ähnlicher Erfahrung können bei uns unterschiedlich verdienen.

3. Wie viel — und wie — wird bei Vogel gearbeitet?

Gemessen wird an dem, was du bewegst, nicht an Stunden. Ehrlich ist aber auch: Wer 9-to-5 sucht, ist bei uns nicht die erste Adresse. Wir suchen Menschen, die aus eigenem Antrieb intensiv arbeiten, weil die Aufgaben es wert sind. Wie du deine Zeit verteilst, ist weitgehend deine Sache. Was wir teilen: Wir arbeiten präsent zusammen — Kultur, Sparring und die besten Ideen entstehen in der täglichen Nähe. Wir sind keine Remote-Company und haben keine großen Home-Office-Policies; einzelne Remote-Tage sind kein Problem.

4. Wie läuft die Bewerbung?

Schlank, schnell, transparent — und nach Profil gestaffelt. Für Einstiegsrollen (Praktikum, Werkstudium, Berufseinstieg) genügen in der Regel zwei Gespräche und eine kurze Arbeitsprobe; erfahrene Rollen laufen etwas ausführlicher. Bei ausgewählten Senior-Rollen prüfen wir, künftig einen gemeinsamen Arbeitstag einzubauen, damit beide Seiten sich besser kennenlernen. Immer gilt: getaktete Termine, zügige Entscheidung, substanzielles Feedback — unabhängig vom Ausgang.

5. Wie funktioniert die variable Vergütung?

Quartalsweise an Leistung gekoppelt, qualitativ bewertet. Die Skala steigt mit dem Level: bis 20 % Associate, 27,5 % Manager, 35 % Senior Manager, 42,5 % Director, 50 % VP. Erwartungswert bei guter Leistung — du erfüllst die Anforderungen, setzt eigene Akzente, bestehst den Keeper Test — liegt bei rund 50 % des Maximums; der Maximalbonus ist nicht der Normalfall. Im Fokus steht eine ganzheitliche Beurteilung durch deine Führungskraft: Ownership, Qualität, Lernkurve, Zusammenarbeit, Impact.

6. Wie entwickle ich mich — welche Karrierewege gibt es?

Zwei aktive Wege: Mastery (fachliche Tiefe, Expertenlaufbahn) und Pioneer (Führung, Management). Die Richtung wählst du nach dem Onboarding, meist in Jahr 1–3. Berufseinstieg ist kein Sonderweg, sondern der frühe Teil derselben Strecke — vom Werkstudenten oder Praktikanten zum Associate, für die Besten ohne erneutes Bewerbungsverfahren.

7. Team, Kultur, Urlaub?

Ein gemeinsames Mittagessen ist ein offenes tägliches Angebot — keine Pflicht; wer mag, kommt dazu, essen kann jeder jederzeit. Dazu Abendessen, Social Events und Offsites in regelmäßigem Rhythmus — nicht als Pflichtprogramm, sondern weil ein gutes Team auch abseits der Arbeit Zeit teilt. Benefits: durchdacht und substanziell, nicht symbolisch. Urlaub: 28 Tage.

8. Ich kenne jemanden — gibt es einen Empfehlungsbonus?

Ja — 2.500 EUR für jede erfolgreich besetzte Stelle (keine Praktika). Kurzer Kontext reicht: an wen du denkst, für welche Rolle, warum. Muss nicht perfekt sitzen, aber substanziell sein.

This is a critical, high-impact role blending policy and procedure definition with operational leadership. You will lead, and scale a high-performing team across Frontline, Second Line, Complaints, Vulnerable Customers and Disputes and be responsible for the customer experience. If you are an experienced leader who thrives on building, scaling, and leading regulated operations, this role is for you.

Core Responsibilities

  • Design and own the end-to-end servicing model - channels, hours, staffing model (in-house, BPO or hybrid), and service-level performance.

  • Establish the Management Information suite that evidences performance to internal stakeholders and regulators.

  • Design and own the complaints policy, procedures and operating model in line with DISP.

  • Build the root-cause reporting, Board-pack Management Information and Consumer Duty outcome monitoring required to evidence good customer outcomes.

  • Design and embed the vulnerable customer framework - covering identification triggers, agent guidance, tailored journeys and assurance.

  • Hire, develop and lead the Customer Support team, scaling capacity ahead of customer growth.

  • Partner with Compliance and Risk as second-line owners of policy sign-off, assurance and regulatory engagement.

  • Partner with Product and Engineering to close the loop from customer feedback and root-cause analysis into the product roadmap.

  • Represent Customer Support to the Board, Risk Committee and the regulator as the named accountable owner.

Qualifications

  • Proven experience building and running customer support in a UK regulated financial services business - banking, e-money, payments, lending or comparable.

  • Deep working knowledge of DISP, FG21/1, the Consumer Duty and FOS processes, as a named owner rather than a consumer of these frameworks.

  • Track record of designing customer operations functions from scratch or leading a material redesign - including policies, MI and operating model.

  • Experience scaling a frontline team through BPO, in-house or hybrid models, with strong command of QA, capacity planning and root-cause discipline.

  • End-to-end ownership of a complaints function, including FOS relationships, and direct experience with chargebacks or scheme disputes.

We work as one team, and we back each other to succeed. So whatever your background or identity, if you’re ready to grow and make a difference, you’ll be right at home here.

It’s important we set you up for success and make our process as accessible as possible. So let us know in your application, or tell your recruiter directly, if you need anything to make your experience or working environment more comfortable.

Life at Checkout.com

We understand that work is just one part of your life. Our hybrid working model offers flexibility, with three days per week in the office to support collaboration and connection.

Curious about what it’s like to be part of our team? Visit our Careers Page to learn more about our culture, open roles, and what drives us.

raw.title: Product Marketing Manager
raw.description:
We're on a mission

Every business grows through a CRM and a direct line to its customers. Healthcare, and pharmacy most of all, is the one place that never happened. It was too hard to build, too hard to distribute, and too hard to do compliantly. Customer data sits idle whilst running a community healthcare business continues to become structurally tighter.

 

We're on a mission to change that. We are the compliant data layer for community healthcare: the system that lets a pharmacy use the patient data it already holds to grow revenue and relationships, compliantly, on the clinical system it already runs.

 

This is already working. Pharmlogic is NHS-assured, integrated and lives in hundreds of pharmacies nationwide, and we've powered millions of patient communications.

 

The role

You will run marketing across the board: brand and social, the website, copy across everything we put out, how we explain the product, and the campaigns that keep our pharmacy customers engaged. You own the channels and you set the standard for how Pharmlogic sounds and looks.

 

You report to the CEO and work closely with the founding team. This is a hands-on role for a generalist who can write, ship, and run several channels at once without waiting to be told. You are early, and the function is yours to shape.

 

The problems you'll own

 

  • Carrying the message: Take our vision, the why behind Pharmlogic, and make it land with the people we exist for. You translate what we believe into words that busy healthcare teams trust and can act on.

  • Communicating in a regulated space: Everything we put out can be read by healthcare professionals, other stakeholders and by patients. You write with the clarity, accuracy and care that demands, where compliant and compelling are the same standard, not a trade-off.

  • Our voice, everywhere: Own how Pharmlogic sounds across social, the website, campaigns and the product itself. One voice, centred on the vision, consistent wherever someone meets us.

  • From product to message: Turn what we build into messaging tailored to all stakeholders in a busy healthcare team that can be immediately understood. You make the complex simple without sacrificing value.

  • The customer journey: Own the communications that take a pharmacy from signed to thriving, engaged, getting full value, and staying, so the story we tell is the experience they have.

  • Knowing what works: Measure what you put out, double down on what performs, and feed what you learn back into how we market, sell and build.

  • Pharmlogic in the room: with the team at sector events, from the stand and the materials to the follow-up, so the people we meet in person get the same clear story as everyone else, and conversations turn into pipeline.

 

This could be for you if

 

  • You're an excellent communicator, above all. Writing is the craft at the centre of this job. You make complex things simple without making them shallow, you have taste, and it shows in everything you put out.

  • You've done lifecycle and product marketing in high-pace SaaS. You know how to take what a product does and turn it into a message people act on, and how to run the journey from signed customer to engaged advocate. That experience is what lets you move fast here from day one.

  • You thrive on the team's success. You get more from a customer win or a teammate's great launch than from your own byline. Small team, shared scoreboard.

  • You share the vision. You believe every healthcare business should be able to understand its customers and improve care for them while staying viable. If that sentence resonates rather than reads as marketing, this will feel like your work, not just a job.

  • You ship at startup pace. You put things out, learn, and go again, rather than polishing one thing for a month, and you do it without waiting for a brief.

  • Tooling fluency helps. Comfort with a CMS, email platforms, CRMs and basic design is a real advantage.

 

What you'll get

You'll be joining a fast-growing company and a small, sharp team focused on making community healthcare thrive.

  • Competitive salary + up to £5,000 in share options

  • Private medical insurance

  • Flexible, hybrid working

  • 28 days of holiday plus bank holidays, and up to 4 weeks a year working from anywhere

you.</li> <li>Experience in restaurant technology, hospitality technology, SaaS platforms, or system integrations is a plus.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Benefits and Perks</strong></p> <ul> <li>Work from The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning. Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its 2025 Design Award winner for Inclusivity.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

About SIMBA Voice Agents by Speechify
 
SIMBA lets companies deploy natural, human-sounding AI voice agents in 71+ languages with sub-second latency. We don't just hand customers a product and wish them luck — every customer gets a Forward Deployed Engineer who builds their agents, joins their Slack, and iterates with them weekly. We're building the future of voice AI, and we're looking for someone who can sell that vision and help bring it to life

About the Role

As an Account Executive / Go-to-Market, you're equal parts dealmaker and builder. You'll own the full sales cycle for new customers — from first call to close — while also getting hands-on during technical evaluations, demos, and early deployment. You understand that selling voice AI isn't just about pitching features; it's about showing prospects exactly how SIMBA fits into their world and making that first integration feel effortless.

This is a rare role for someone who can command a boardroom and open a terminal.

What You'll Do

  • Own the full sales cycle from prospecting through close for mid-market and enterprise accounts
  • Run technically deep discovery calls to understand customer use cases, tech stack, and integration requirements
  • Build and demo custom voice agent prototypes during the sales process to accelerate buy-in
  • Partner with Forward Deployed Engineers to ensure a seamless handoff from sale to onboarding
  • Develop GTM playbooks, messaging, and outbound strategies to help SIMBA break into new verticals
  • Represent customer needs internally, influencing product roadmap and packaging decisions
  • Maintain a clean pipeline in CRM and accurately forecast revenue
What We're Looking For
  • 3–6 years of experience in a sales, account executive, or GTM role at a technical B2B company
  • Track record of closing deals with both technical buyers (CTOs, engineers) and business stakeholders
  • Comfortable getting hands-on with APIs and no-code/low-code tools to build compelling demos
  • Strong understanding of the AI/ML or voice technology landscape — you follow this space closely
  • Exceptional communicator who can simplify complex technical concepts without losing their depth
  • Highly self-directed with strong pipeline discipline and a bias toward action
Nice to Have
  • Experience selling AI, voice, or conversational technology
  • Familiarity with telephony infrastructure, contact centers, or customer experience platforms
  • Prior experience in a forward deployment or solutions engineering capacity
  • Multilingual or experience selling into international markets
Why Speechify SIMBA
  • Sell a product that genuinely impresses prospects — sub-second latency and 71+ languages speaks for itself
  • High ownership role with direct input on GTM strategy and positioning
  • Work alongside a team that stays embedded with customers, so you're never selling something that doesn't deliver
  • Competitive base + commission, equity, and benefits
  • Fast-moving startup environment where your wins have outsized impact

And don't forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Refer them!

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its 2025 Design Award winner for Inclusivity.  

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies

What You'll Do
  • Lead the design, architecture, and development of native Windows desktop applications using Windows App SDK, WinUI (or related UI frameworks), C#, XAML, and — when needed — C++.
  • Define and enforce best-practices for Windows desktop development across the codebase: code architecture, performance, memory usage, responsive UI, cross-version compatibility (Windows 10/11+), and maintainability.
  • Drive accessibility efforts: integrate and validate support for accessibility APIs (e.g. Microsoft UI Automation or other relevant Windows accessibility frameworks), ensure UI controls, focus management, keyboard navigation, screen-reader support, and usability for users with disabilities.
  • Collaborate closely with product designers, UX researchers, QA, and other stakeholders to shape feature planning, UI/UX architecture, and long-term roadmap for the Windows platform.
  • Take ownership of full lifecycle of features: conception → design → implementation → testing → release → maintenance. Ensure quality, reliability, and consistency across releases.
  • Identify, diagnose, and resolve complex bugs, performance bottlenecks, memory leaks, rendering issues, or compatibility problems — and propose robust architectural or design solutions.
 
An ideal candidate should have

Required:

  • 3+ in Windows desktop application development using Windows App SDK, WinUI (or similar), C#, XAML — and ideally additional experience with native Windows code (C++, Win32/WinRT/COM).
  • Deep understanding of Windows application architecture, including interop between managed code (.NET) and native code.
  • Proven track record of designing, building, and shipping production-quality desktop applications, with an emphasis on reliability, performance, scalability, and maintainability.
  • Strong experience with accessibility APIs on Windows (e.g. Microsoft UI Automation or similar), and a dedication to building accessible and inclusive software.
  • Excellent software engineering fundamentals: OOP, design patterns, data structures, algorithms, memory management, multi-threading or asynchronous programming (where relevant).
  • Experience leading technical design, mentoring other engineers, conducting code reviews, and making architecture-level decisions.
  • Strong communication skills; ability to articulate tradeoffs, collaborate with cross-functional teams, and drive consensus.
  • A user-centric mindset: focus on building polished, intuitive, and accessible experiences for end users.

Preferred / Bonus:

  • Experience with writing automated tests for UI — unit tests, integration tests, UI automation tests; familiarity with relevant testing frameworks.
  • Experience with performance optimization for desktop apps (memory usage, startup time, rendering performance, high-DPI support, responsiveness under load).
  • Experience with localization/globalization, right-to-left UI support, internationalization, accessibility for multiple regions.
  • Familiarity with telemetry, analytics, crash reporting, logging, and error monitoring in desktop applications.
  • Previous experience in shaping CI/CD workflows, release pipelines, and deployment strategies for desktop applications.
  • Demonstrated ability to take ownership of feature areas or modules and drive them long-term, including maintenance, refactoring, and technical debt management.

What we offer

  • A high-impact role: you will define architecture, shape the future of our Windows product, and directly influence what millions of users see and experience.
  • A collaborative, flat-structure engineering culture — you are not just a coder, but a builder and a decision-maker.
  • Opportunities to lead — mentor others, steer technical direction, and grow into broader technical leadership (e.g. Tech Lead, Architect).
  • Flexibility, autonomy, and responsibility: you define how to solve problems, own features end-to-end, and contribute to long-term product vision.
  • A purpose-driven mission: building software that's reliable, accessible, and user-centered — making a real difference for people.

The Product Assurance team at CoMind is responsible for ensuring the device performs as intended against its specified requirements, generating the test evidence needed to support regulatory submissions and design history files. Working across hardware, software, and integrated system levels, the team designs and executes test methods and protocols that demonstrate design outputs meet design inputs to the standard required for FDA clearance and CE marking.

You will develop test protocols, validate the test methods and equipment, execute testing, analyse and collate results, and author reports for a regulated medical device, working closely with systems engineering and quality throughout.   2. The $2T European healthcare market is overlooked by the most talented builders.

Our master plan:

  • Step 0 → $100M/yr by end of 2025: We went from $10M to $100M in 6 months serving the UK GLP-1 market.

  • Step 1 → $1B ARR by end of 2026: Over the last 12 months we've grown from 3k to 150k UK active GLP-1 patients. We’ll continue this growth curve to hit $1B ARR.

  • Step 2 → $10B ARR by end of 2028: Blitzscale Europe. We’ll be Europe’s largest GLP-1 provider.

  • Step 3 → $100B/yr by end of 2031: Get regulatory approval across Europe for our Full Autonomous Prescribing (FAP) system. Win contracts at scale with European payers to mass replace human labor. We’ll be the dominant full-stack AI doctor in Europe.

  • Step 4 → $1T/yr by end of 2035: With one line of code and zero human time, you can use AIOS to treat any patient globally with any medication.

In so doing, we’ll become the world’s first trillion-dollar healthcare company.

We’re a young, founder-led company. This is still Day 1 and all our work is ahead of us.

You can read more about working with us here: Working at AIOS

Being a Clinical Pharmacist at AIOS

We are building a world-class team.

At AIOS Tech (Bolt Pharmacy), we're building the world's first full-stack AI doctor. Right now it's akin to assisted self-driving (and improving every day), so humans are prescribing with AI assisting their workflows.

You'll join our growing team of Independent Prescribers, working through GLP-1 weight-management consultations day in, day out. You understand that a great patient experience means catching everything you need to prescribe safely and confidently first time - not sending someone back and forth for information you should have picked up on intake.

You'll assess each patient on their own merits: the comorbidity, the interacting medication, the case that needs a second look, and make the right call. You’ll never compromise on safety or accuracy.

You'll:

  • Deliver safe, evidence-based GLP-1 prescribing for every patient on your list

  • Take full ownership of the clinical quality, safety and accuracy of your own consultations and records

  • Flag anything that needs escalating—a red flag, a near miss, a protocol gap—clearly and quickly

  • Follow, and help sharpen, our clinical protocols as they evolve

This role is suited to a confident, forward-thinking prescriber with sound clinical judgement, excellent attention to detail, and a strong commitment to patient safety.

Great performance in this role means your patients are safe, your records hold up to audit, and you're working through a full, steady caseload without ever cutting corners. If you nail this role, you'll be a strong candidate for more senior clinical positions as we grow.

This is an ongoing contractor engagement - full-time (40h) preferred, part-time (20h+) available - fully remote/WFH or hybrid onsite in Blackburn.

You’ll report directly to your team lead.

You’ll also work most closely with:

  • Saim Dalvi (UK Clinical Lead)

  • Mobeen Nawaz (Interim Clinical Ops Lead)

  • Phuong Nguyen (Superintendent Pharmacist)

Key Responsibilities

  • Prescribing: Deliver safe, evidence-based GLP-1 prescribing for every patient you see — assessing suitability, comorbidities and contraindications before you write anything.

  • Consultations: Run detailed, efficient consultations that capture everything you need the first time, so patients aren't stuck in back-and-forth messiness.

  • Monitoring: Track treatment response and side effects across your caseload, and adjust care promptly and safely.

  • Escalation: Recognise what's outside your remit, and escalate red flags, near misses or complex cases to your Senior Clinician Team Lead quickly and clearly.

  • Documentation: Keep accurate, concise and contemporaneous clinical records that hold up to audit.

  • Governance: Contribute to clinical audits, incident learning and quality improvement when asked.

  • Collaboration: Work smoothly with customer support, operational and technology teams to keep the service safe and moving in service of our patient base.

Need to Have

  • Registration: GPhC-registered pharmacist with an Independent Prescriber (IP) annotation, held for at least 1 year.

  • GLP-1 Confidence: You've prescribed weight-management, GLP-1s or a closely related area — comorbidities and polypharmacy don't throw you off protocol.

  • Clinical Reasoning: You think clearly and quickly within a protocol-led service.

  • Safety Mindset: Patient safety and quality are non-negotiable for you. Red flags don't get past you.

  • Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication, including confident patient counselling.

  • Pace: Comfortable in a fast-paced, high-volume, protocol-led environment, and you don't let volume compromise accuracy.

  • Digital Literacy: Confident using electronic health records and remote consultation platforms.

  • Flexibility: Willing to support evening or weekend rotas when needed. With sufficient notice, you work the hours that our patients need you to work so they can be served without long wait times and unnecessary friction.

Nice to Have

  • Consultation Modes: Experience with asynchronous, telephone and/or video consultations.

  • Specialist Training: Additional training in obesity or weight management, such as SCOPE certification.

  • Postgraduate: A postgraduate clinical diploma or equivalent.

  • Complex Patients: Comfortable managing patients with diabetes, cardiovascular disease, renal impairment or polypharmacy.

  • Governance Experience: Some experience contributing to clinical audits, incident investigations or quality-improvement projects.

  • Protocols: Exposure to developing SOPs, clinical protocols or prescribing pathways.

  • Startup Pace: Experience working in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, ideally in the weight loss space.

  • Growth Mindset: An interest in eventually mentoring or supporting more junior colleagues as you grow with us.

  • Systems: Familiarity with clinical support and customer management systems.

    🎯 “You just build a f*ing amazing experience. Make each step amazing. Make every decision in the long term interest of the customer. Give the customer massively more value than you take.”

Training and onboarding

  • Training is delivered completely remotely

  • The duration of training is a minimum of 2 days, with scheduling negotiable depending on experience and prior exposure to GLP-1 prescribing or digital health services.

  • Ongoing mentoring and support are provided throughout your induction and practice.

You get paid above market salary and you get early stage equity, so you get really rich if we nail this.

    • Building robust, fault-tolerant systems
